Measure the control height and record it against the printed band (MAX 6" at the control location per A532.1 view 02; MIN 8" / MAX 10" above the rim per A532 elevation 05, tub configuration). Read and WRITE DOWN the valve and cartridge model actually installed — the guestroom rows name none.

label: CONFIGURATION B (ROLL-IN SHOWER) - Shower diverter valve (kn 10) — applies only if the roll-in was built
where: Roll-in shower control wall at 118, alongside the pressure-balancing valve. Tagged on A532 elevation 02 and A532.1 views 01 and 02.
src: A532 elevation 02 · A532.1 views 01 and 02 · A530 BATHROOM KEYED NOTE 10
verifyAtPunch: Only if the roll-in was built. Move the diverter through its full travel: it must move positively between the fixed head and the hand shower and HOLD there under full flow without creeping back. With it set to the hand shower, confirm the fixed head STOPS completely — any dribble from the head is cross-flow and is the finding. Measure the diverter height and record it with the other controls.

label: CONFIGURATION B (ROLL-IN SHOWER) - Hand shower and side bar (keyed note 11) — the handset's on/off control MUST be NON-POSITIVE shut-off; hose MIN 59" long and slide-bar top 4'-0 1/2" MAX (G402 det 02)
where: Roll-in shower wall at 118 on a slide bar. A532.1 view 02 prints 3'-6", 2'-10", 2'-8", 1'-5", 1'-3", 1'-0" and MAX 6" at the control zone; grab-bar band MIN 33" / MAX 36". Also carried on view 03, the folding-seat wall.
src: A532.1 views 02 and 03 keyed note 11 · A530 BATHROOM KEYED NOTE 11 (verbatim: 'HAND SHOWER AND SIDE BAR. HAND-HELD SHOWER UNIT REQUIRED TO HAVE ON/OFF CONTROL WITH NON-POSITIVE SHUT OFF.') · G402 detail 02 ACCESSIBLE SHOWER, 'BACK' wall (verbatim 'SHOWER HOSE TO BE MIN. 59" LONG'; slide-bar top 4'-0 1/2" MAX; controls in the hatched zone 2'-3" MAX / 1'-4" MIN off the seat wall) · A533 view 04 keyed note 11 (a TUB elevation, on a different room type — see note)
verifyAtPunch: If the roll-in was built: slide the handset the full length of the bar and confirm it locks at any height and does not slip under the weight of the hose; push and pull on the bar — solid to blocking, no movement. MEASURE and record the hose length against MIN 59" and the top of the slide bar against 4'-0 1/2" MAX (G402 det 02). CRITICAL: operate the handset's OWN on/off control and confirm it does NOT fully shut off flow (A530 kn 11 requires NON-POSITIVE shut-off). A handset that shuts flow off dead is the wrong unit even though it looks right on the wall — photograph it and log the model. Confirm the hose reaches the seat position. IF A TUB WAS BUILT INSTEAD: still record present or absent with a photo — A532's tub elevations omit kn 11 but A533's tub elevation carries it, so an absence here is evidence for the open RFI, not yet a defect.

label: CONFIGURATION B (ROLL-IN SHOWER) - Shower enclosure with tempered-glass door (kn 5) — GLASS SUB scope, not plumbing
where: Roll-in shower opening at 118. kn 5 is placed on A552 plan 01; A530 kn 27 additionally requires door-stop hardware at the shower glass.
src: A552 plan 01 kn 5 ('SHOWER ENCLOSURE W/ TEMPERED GLASS DOOR') · A530 kn 27 (door-stop hardware)
verifyAtPunch: Only if the roll-in was built. Panels move through their full travel without binding; check plumb and parallel with a level at both jambs. Find and photograph the tempered stamp on the glass. Run water at the door for two minutes and confirm nothing escapes at the jambs, track or sill. Confirm the door-stop hardware required by A530 kn 27 is fitted so the back-of-door hardware cannot strike the glass when fully ajar. Bill this to the glass sub, not to Larry's Plumbing.

label: Floor drain, guest bathroom — 2" per the P301-series general notes; "MAINTAIN ACCESSIBLE COMPLIANT SLOPES TO DRAIN". No guestroom floor drain is scheduled anywhere in P104
where: Bath floor at/near the shower. On 118 keynote 6 'FLOOR DRAIN' is drawn TWICE on A552 — on architectural plan 01 and again on finish plan 03.
src: A552 plan 01 kn 6 and finish plan 03 kn 6 · A530 kn 20 · P402 ('floor drain in accessible units') · P301 general note (FD 2")
verifyAtPunch: Strainer secure and flush with the tile, not proud and not dished — run a straightedge across it. Pour a cup of water at each corner of the bath floor in turn and watch each reach the drain; nothing may pond. Confirm the floor slope does not exceed 1:48 in any direction (G402 bath GN4). Pour water into the drain and confirm the trap holds a seal. RECORD the make, model and strainer finish you find — no guestroom floor drain is scheduled anywhere in P104 (FD-1/FD-2/FD-3 are Mech/Laundry, Unfinished and Funnel), so your record is the product answer.

label: Trap guard / trap primer at the bathroom floor drain — the primer valve body is concealed but the trap guard is visible through the strainer and the seal is testable
where: At the guest-bath floor drain. The primer valve body is concealed; P102 requires primers in ACCESSIBLE locations per NPCA / ASSE 1018.
src: P301 general note 6 ('All floor drains to be installed with trap guards / primers', repeated P302–P310) · P501 detail 12 · P102 Automatic Trap Primer Valve Schedule (Sioux Chief 695) · P104 Water Appurtenance Schedule TP-1 (PPP SMP-500-115V)
verifyAtPunch: Lift the strainer and look into the drain body: is a trap guard fitted, yes or no? Record it. Pour water in, then confirm the seal holds. Ask housekeeping to leave the room unused and re-check on the next pass for a dry trap or sewer odour — a dry trap on the second pass is the finding. If a primer line is visible, trace it and record whether its valve is reachable (P102 requires primers in ACCESSIBLE locations per NPCA / ASSE 1018).

label: Gate valves at the CWS, HWS and HWR riser take-offs — one at each of the three risers, with unions, behind an 18"x18" access panel
where: Guestroom wet wall / plumbing stack. WHERE THE PANEL PHYSICALLY LANDS IS THE OPEN QUESTION — see note.
src: P401 Domestic Water Typical Unit (GV at each of the three riser take-offs) · P502 detail 3 Shut-Off Valve Installation Detail · P101 general note 9 and general note 15 · M101 GN7
verifyAtPunch: Find the 18"x18" access panel and RECORD WHERE IT IS (guestroom ceiling / bath ceiling / corridor outside the door) with a photo. Open it and cycle all three valves — CWS, HWS and HWR — fully closed and fully open, confirming each actually stops flow at the fixture it serves; no weep at any stem afterwards. RECORD whether the valves are GATE (P401 / P502 det 3) or BALL (P101 GN15) — both are drawn and the sheets do not agree. Confirm a union at each. If there is NO panel anywhere, write that up as the finding.

label: PTAC condensate drain — 1" VISIBLE drain with 1" air-gap fitting, 1-1/2" vent up, Type M copper, to the 4" condensate main
where: At the PTAC on the window wall, running down the wall (M501 det.9). Where the air-gap fitting physically lands is NOT stated by any sheet.
src: P301 / P302 ('1" visible condensate drain for each A/C unit (typ.), provide 1" air gap fitting') · P501 detail 13 · M401 KN2 · M501 det.9 · P102 material schedule
verifyAtPunch: Run the PTAC in cooling long enough to make condensate (15-20 min on a warm day), then look: no standing water in the base pan, no drip inside the room, no stain at the sleeve, wall, carpet edge or the ST-01 stool. Trace the visible 1" drain down the wall and confirm the 1" air-gap fitting is present, open and not taped, painted or packed shut; RECORD where the air-gap fitting physically lands (in the room / in the chase / at the exterior) — no sheet places it. Confirm the visible piping is copper, not PVC glued into a copper run. Name the trade before you walk: condensate is plumbing (M401 KN2, M501 det.9), the PTAC is HVAC.

label: Kitchenette / wet-bar sink and faucet — NO product scheduled in P104; procured per S4: American Standard PEKOE 23x18 single-bowl stainless undermount 18SB.10231800.075 + Moen 8227
where: Entry / kitchenette leg if provided — A552 gives the kitchenette leg 7'-10 1/2" CLEAR. A552 tags 901 REFRIGERATOR and 902 DISHWASHER on the working wall and tags NO SINK.
src: P401 and P402 (mark SK-3 / SK-4, 'in the suite/extended units') · P104 (schedules NO product for either mark) · P201 riser #P2 (an SK on a guestroom stack) · S4 product data
verifyAtPunch: Record PRESENT or ABSENT in the kitchenette leg — that answer alone closes half the open question. If present: undermount clips tight with no sag along the front edge, bottom grid fitted, faucet hot-left with full travel and no drip. Fill the bowl and drain it, then wipe the trap and both stops with tissue — dry or it is a weep. Confirm the dishwasher (902) drain is connected and there is a high loop or air gap. RECORD the faucet make, model and the deck hole pattern: the S4 file titled 'Moen Kitchenette Faucet' is on its own product sheet an 8" widespread 3-HOLE LAVATORY faucet, which will not drop into a single-hole kitchenette deck — if that is what arrived, photograph it. Do not raise a second RFI; one is already open.

label: P-trap cover and supply-line wrap at the ACCESSIBLE lavatory — G400 det 06: 'WRAP EXPOSED HOT WATER PIPES AND DRAIN W/ PROTECTIVE PIPE COVER'; G402 det 05: 'PROTECT DRAIN TRAP AND SUPPLY LINES AGAINST CONTACT PER ACCESSIBILITY GUIDELINES'; TA 24 / TA 25 P-trap covers
where: In the knee space under the accessible lavatory at 118 (A532/A532.1 kn 8, 'CLEAR AREA OF SINK/VANITY MUST BE ACCESSIBLE').
src: G400 detail 06 (ACCESSIBLE SINK front view: 'WRAP EXPOSED HOT WATER PIPES AND DRAIN W/ PROTECTIVE PIPE COVER') · G400 and G402 TA schedule rows TA 24 (P-TRAP COVER AT BUILT IN VANITIES) and TA 25 (P-TRAP COVER AT WALL HUNG SINKS) — identical 40-row schedule printed on both sheets · G402 detail 05 (verbatim leader 'PROTECT DRAIN TRAP AND SUPPLY LINES AGAINST CONTACT PER ACCESSIBILITY GUIDELINES') and detail 04 (section, PIPE WRAP callout, 2'-3" MIN CLEAR knee, 8" MIN knee depth, 11" MIN toe depth) · A532 / A532.1 kn 8 (clear area of sink/vanity must be accessible) · coordination_issues C-09 [note: C-09's 'one sheet only' finding is stale — G400 was not in its search list]
verifyAtPunch: Reach into the knee space under the lavatory the way a seated guest would: the P-trap must be wrapped or covered and BOTH supply lines insulated so nothing hot or abrasive can be touched. Run the tap hot for 60 s and then put the back of your hand on each covered line — you must not feel heat through the wrap. Confirm nothing sharp or unfinished projects into the clear area. Bare pipes, or wrap on the drain only, is a write-up.
